hints: Expand sin(x+45°) and collect the sine and cosine coefficients.
Match them with Rcos(x−α)=Rcosα cosx+Rsinα sinx.
Use the coefficient pair to find R and α in 0°<α<90°, giving α to 1 decimal place.
walkthrough:
Expand $\sin(x + 45^{\circ})$ using the compound angle formula $\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$:
$$\sin(x + 45^{\circ}) = \sin x\cos(45^{\circ}) + \cos x\sin(45^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin x + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos x$$

Multiply by $3\sqrt{2}$ and add $\cos x$:
$$3\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin x + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos x\right) + \cos x = (3\sin x + 3\cos x) + \cos x = 4\cos x + 3\sin x$$

Equate with $R\cos(x - \alpha) = R\cos x\cos\alpha + R\sin x\sin\alpha$:
$$R\cos\alpha = 4$$
$$R\sin\alpha = 3$$

Calculate $R$ by squaring and adding:
$$R^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 = 16 + 9 = 25 \implies R = \sqrt{25} = 5$$

hints: Use part (a) with x=3θ to turn the equation into one cosine equation.
Convert back to θ, retain every value in 0°<θ<180°, and give degree answers to 1 decimal place.
walkthrough:
Substitute $x = 3\theta$ into the identity from part (a):
$$3\sqrt{2}\sin(3\theta + 45^{\circ}) + \cos(3\theta) = 5\cos(3\theta - 36.87^{\circ})$$
$$5\cos(3\theta - 36.87^{\circ}) = -4$$
$$\cos(3\theta - 36.87^{\circ}) = -\dfrac{4}{5} = -0.8$$

Find the principal inverse cosine angle:
$$\cos^{-1}(-0.8) \approx 143.13^{\circ}$$

Establish the domain for the angle $3\theta - 36.87^{\circ}$ given $0^{\circ} < \theta < 180^{\circ}$:
$$0^{\circ} < 3\theta < 540^{\circ} \implies -36.87^{\circ} < 3\theta - 36.87^{\circ} < 503.13^{\circ}$$

Solve for possible angles in this range:
$$\text{First solution: } 3\theta - 36.87^{\circ} = 143.13^{\circ}$$
$$3\theta = 143.13^{\circ} + 36.87^{\circ} = 180.00^{\circ} \implies \theta = \dfrac{180.00^{\circ}}{3} = 60.0^{\circ}$$
$$\text{Second solution: } 3\theta - 36.87^{\circ} = 360^{\circ} - 143.13^{\circ} = 216.87^{\circ}$$
$$3\theta = 216.87^{\circ} + 36.87^{\circ} = 253.74^{\circ} \implies \theta = \dfrac{253.74^{\circ}}{3} = 84.58^{\circ} \approx 84.6^{\circ}$$

State all solutions in the interval $0^{\circ} < \theta < 180^{\circ}$ correct to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 60.0^{\circ}, \quad 84.6^{\circ}$$
